items.title: The Arab Kingmaker in Israel’s Election Who Wants a Partnership With Jews
items.summary: Mansour Abbas, a dentist-turned-lawmaker, helped oust Benjamin Netanyahu once before. Now, he and a Jewish ex-police commander have teamed up to try to do it again.

items.title: The Rupturing Trump-Zelensky Relationship Stands to Hurt Ukraine and Its European Allies
items.summary: Where the two presidents’ war of words will end is anybody’s guess. But if it continues, it could threaten the crucial operational help that Ukraine still gets from the United States.

items.title: Israeli Settlers Attack Palestinians and Washington Post Journalist in West Bank
items.summary: In the latest surge of violence, settlers targeted Palestinians during the olive harvest, a cultural touchstone and economic lifeline in the Israeli-occupied area.

items.title: Pope Asks Putin for a Cease-Fire for a Ukrainian City Under Siege
items.summary: Recovering from lung cancer surgery, Pope Leo XIV spoke with Vladimir V. Putin to make a plea for Oleshky, where mines and drones have trapped some 2,000 people who are at risk of starvation.

items.title: Deadly School Roof Collapse in Pakistan Raises Questions Over Regulation
items.summary: A roof collapse that killed 32 children and a teacher in northwest Pakistan has prompted safety inspections of schools across the region.

items.title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia Put In Doubt Kingdom’s Sports and Business Events
items.summary: The Iran-backed group’s attacks have disrupted sports tournaments and threatened business events that the kingdom has long used to attract investment and raise its profile.

items.title: Caracas Is Eerily Safe After Deadly Police Raids in Venezuela Killed Thousands
items.summary: Crime plunged after police raids killed thousands. Venezuela is now withdrawing from the International Criminal Court as it investigates this blood-soaked campaign.

items.title: What Life Is Like in Kyiv as Russia Tries to Make It Unlivable
items.summary: A day in the Ukrainian capital, a new kind of battlefield far from the front, where daily life means assessing — and accepting — deadly risks.

items.title: El Niño Threatens Global Sugar Supply
items.summary: A sugarcane crop withered by El Niño in India, the world’s second-largest producer, is hurting consumers and farmers — plus undermining the country’s energy security goals.

items.title: The Sexual Abuse Crisis in Paris’s Public Schools
items.summary: A surge of abuse accusations has led Parisian authorities to acknowledge a “collective failure” to prevent sexual offenders from working in schools.

items.title: M.L.B. Playoff Ads With Sydney Sweeney and Megan Fox Draw Backlash
items.summary: Commercials with Sydney Sweeney promoting a gambling platform and Megan Fox endorsing male enhancement have rankled fans, and even athletes. Who is in charge?

items.title: Netflix Hurries to Rewrite Its Narrative With Layoffs and a Sudden Firing
items.summary: Despite strong revenues and profits, the streaming service cut 1,000 jobs and jettisoned its chief content officer. Drops in the stock price and viewer engagement are to blame.

items.title: U.S. Budget Deficit Nears $2 Trillion, a Reality Check for Trump’s Cost Cutting
items.summary: Higher interest rates are inflating borrowing costs as the Trump administration spends on the Iran war and tariff refunds.

items.title: You’ve Found a Long-Lost CD. Can You Still Get Your Money?
items.summary: The bank was required to hold the certificate of deposit only for a limited time, and now has no record of the money. Experts offer tips to avoid having this happen to you.

items.title: When Will the Fed Move on Rates?
items.summary: Kevin Warsh, the central bank’s chairman, suggested he wouldn’t push to raise borrowing rates this month. But persistent inflation may force the Fed’s hand.

items.title: Indonesian Stocks Plunge as MSCI Threatens to Drop Market from Indexes
items.summary: The potential downgrade by MSCI, an influential index provider, adds to a deepening crisis of investor confidence in the economic policies of President Prabowo Subianto.

items.title: Feel Like You’re Overpaying for Hotels? Blame Expedia, a New Lawsuit Says.
items.summary: The booking giant is accused of breaking federal antitrust laws and forcing millions of customers to overspend on stays by as much as 30 percent.

items.title: Lufthansa’s Final A346 Flight Marks the End of an Aviation Love Story
items.summary: Lufthansa’s quirky plane, with its extra-long fuselage, four engines and restrooms down a flight of stairs, has a devoted following. Now, the carrier, one of few still flying the model, is taking it out of service.

items.title: Trump Hasn’t Lowered Drug Prices for These Voters
items.summary: President Trump has been promoting his efforts to reduce drug prices, but many Americans have not seen relief from rising costs for prescriptions and insurance premiums.

items.title: After Welcoming China’s Electric Vehicles, This Country Is Paying the Price
items.summary: Thailand introduced subsidies and tax cuts to encourage electric vehicle adoption. Now it is trying to recalibrate, alarmed by the threat to its industrial landscape.

items.title: Meta Withdraws $25 Million from Its Midterms Push
items.summary: The company outlined a $65 million budget last year when it embarked on an effort to elect state politicians friendly to the A.I. industry.

items.title: OpenAI Engineer, Who Is Charged With Planting Bug, Advised Saudis
items.summary: The employee, now fired, had said he advised government agencies in Saudi Arabia. He was also listed as a partner at a venture firm with a Saudi prince.

items.title: Why No One Can Look Away From Elizabeth Holmes
items.summary: “I felt like there were some moments in the film where she was just brazenly lying.”

items.title: Ms., Martians and Guacamole: Their First Time in The Times
items.summary: Our reporters share a compendium of debuts, discoveries and (sometimes overdue) appearances in the paper.

items.title: Exhausted Parents Are Turning to A.I. Apps Despite the Risks
items.summary: Even as alarm grows over the risks, families are embracing bots and agents to tackle the spiraling administrative tasks of modern child rearing.

items.title: Tesla Debuts 2026 Roadster ‘Flying’ Electric Sports Car
items.summary: Elon Musk’s company and other automakers, like Jaguar and Bentley, are trying to sell very expensive electric cars to people who usually prefer gasoline-fueled luxury and performance.

items.title: Anthropic Says Revenue Jumped 45% to $16.8 Billion in Third Quarter
items.summary: The company held an investor meeting on Wednesday as it plans a blockbuster initial public offering as soon as next month.

items.title: Netflix, Facing Slowing Growth, Cuts 6% of Its Work Force
items.summary: The streamer’s share price is down more than 40 percent over the last year as the company has struggled with stalling engagement.

items.title: Senators Question Meta’s Data Center Tax Strategy
items.summary: Democrats on the Senate Finance Committee sent a letter to Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s chief executive, questioning the company’s $6.6 billion in tax breaks.

items.title: Rogue A.I. Agents from China Chatted with Researchers
items.summary: Researchers discovered that the agents were trying to bypass security controls on websites and made contact with them. A Times reporter was invited to join the discussion.
